alternatives.option: Exempt evidence_class human_ruling from the ancestor-membership check
alternatives.reason_rejected: human_ruling is the highest-authority class; exempting it from the capability check is precisely the R03/R17 hole the class system exists to close

alternatives.option: Have admission fall back to the replica's latest policy when the ancestry is empty
alternatives.reason_rejected: directly contradicts D29, which was adopted because rebuild dropped an admitted event otherwise

context: Merged lane/03-runtime into foundation/v3; resolved the events-verb collision between lanes 02c and 03, and fixed the signing ceremony producing rulings its own admission rule quarantined.
rationale: Lane 03's appendRuling created principal -> membership -> ruling but linked none of them, so under lane 02b's ancestor-membership rule the ruling had no policy in its ancestry and was quarantined no_policy_yet. The ceremony was producing output its own store could not admit. The membership event id (or, for an existing policy, the projected record's `version`, which is the latest admitted event on that record) is now passed as a parent alongside the principal event that introduces the signing key. This is the mechanism working as designed rather than a relaxation: an event that cites no policy genuinely cannot be judged against one.
summary: Made the signing ceremony cite the membership it establishes as a causal parent of the ruling it mints
